newsitem.title: POLAND: Four investment groups seek Polish PZU stake.
newsitem.headline: Four investment groups seek Polish PZU stake.

text.p: Poland's largest insurance firm, Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA, is holding talks with four foreign and domestic groups to buy shares in PZU during its privatisation expected at the end of July, a PZU official said.

PZU spokesman Marek Maszek told Reuters on Wednesday that an information memorandum on PZU had been sent to 21 interested parties in June grouped in four teams seeking shares in the planned closed issue worth 500-600 million zlotys.
"(The potential investors) have formed four groups and four large consulting firms are talking with us in their name," Maszek said, adding that the July sale target was not binding.

Maszek declined to give names of the interested potential investors but press reports have said the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and state-owned Bank Pekao SA have expressed interest.
Maszek said the financial condition of the potential investors, their ability to provide synergistic effects and their willingness to stay with PZU in the long term would be taken into consideration.

The state treasury has said it would keep more than 50 percent of the firm, which holds two-thirds of the Polish non-life insurance market, and that investors could buy share packages of 10 to 15 percent.

Last month PZU's president said the firm made a net profit of 204.9 million zlotys in 1997's first quarter an expected a profit this year despite last year's 170-million-zloty net loss and technical loss of 345 million zlotys.
